**AutoMetrik** is an all-in-one management software designed specifically for **auto repair shops** and service centers. It functions as a comprehensive Enterprise Resource Planning (ERP) system, centralizing every aspect of your repair business—from the moment a vehicle enters the bay to the final payment.

With AutoMetrik, you can streamline your entire service workflow. You can effortlessly create professional **estimates**, convert them into active **job orders**, and generate accurate **invoices** and **payments**.

Crucially, AutoMetrik gives you full control over your stock. It allows you to **track inventory** in real-time and manage **purchase orders**, ensuring you always know exactly what parts and materials are on hand and what needs to be replenished.

AutoMetrik empowers your shop to:

  - **Master Your Financials:** Automatically generate detailed **sales reports** and **financial statements** so you always understand your shop’s profitability and cash flow.

  - **Boost Customer Retention:** Send automated **customer service reminders** for preventive maintenance, keeping your clients coming back.

  - **Streamline Daily Operations:** From tracking employee tasks to managing supplier relationships, everything is organized in one dashboard.

  - **Access Data Anywhere:** Because it’s cloud-based, you can log into AutoMetrik from any device with internet access, giving you control over your shop even when you’re away from the office.

AutoMetrik brings together everything your repair shop needs—saving you time, reducing errors, and helping your team work more efficiently.

AutoMetrik is designed for **all types of automotive businesses**—whether you're running a small car dealership or managing a large automotive company with multiple locations. No matter the size of your business, AutoMetrik provides the tools you need to stay organized and operate efficiently.

It’s a flexible platform built specifically for the **automotive industry**, helping businesses handle their daily tasks like tracking car inventory, managing customer and supplier relationships, monitoring expenses, and coordinating employee activities.

Because it’s cloud-based, there’s no need for expensive hardware or complex setups. This makes AutoMetrik a smart choice for **small businesses that need an affordable, easy-to-use solution**, as well as **larger companies that require more advanced features and scalability**.

Whether you sell a few cars a week or manage hundreds of vehicles across multiple branches, AutoMetrik adapts to your needs and grows with your business.

The system is a powerful and easy-to-use management platform built specifically for businesses in the automotive industry—whether you’re running a small workshop or managing a large dealership. Designed to support daily operations, AutoMetrik helps streamline key business functions like inventory control, financial tracking, customer management, and service operations.

  - **Dashboard Overview:** Provides a centralized view of business metrics, including Profit & Loss, Job Orders, Customers, Inventory, and Vehicles.

  - **Financial Management:** Tracks revenue and expenses, with breakdowns for revenue sources (Parts and Accessories, Service Income, etc.) and expenses (Bank Charges, etc.). Displays cash flow and 6-month sales trends.

  - **Inventory Tracking:** Monitors stock levels, aiding in stock management for parts and accessories.

  - **Customer and Vehicle Management:** Manages customer data and vehicle statuses supporting job order and service tracking.

  - **Reporting and Analytics:** Offers visual insights via pie charts (Revenue Breakdown) and line graphs (6-Month Sales), helping analyze financial performance over time.

  - **Operational Tools:** Includes sections for Product Inquiry, Operations, CRM, and Accounting, suggesting capabilities for customer relations, job scheduling, and financial record-keeping.

These features indicate AutoMetrik is a comprehensive auto shop management tool focused on financial oversight, inventory control, and operational efficiency.

At the top of the screen, the system features a top bar that includes Qonnec branding to indicate the system or **company name**, **a search icon** for quick access to records, and a **user profile section** which contains user settings, logout options, or profile management features. The system also includes a **collapsible side navigation panel** on the left side of the screen that acts as the main navigation menu. This panel can be opened or closed to help you quickly find and access the tools and information you need. Below is a simple explanation of each section in the navigation panel:

  - **Dashboard:** This is the main page you see when you log in. It gives you a quick overview of important business details, such as profits, sales, and summaries of your work, all in one place.

  - **Vehicles:** This section lets you manage information about the vehicles in your shop. You can view and update details about the cars you’re working on.

  - **Customers:** Use this section to keep track of your customers’ information. It helps you manage their details and add new customers as needed.

  - **Product Inquiry:** This area is likely for looking up details about products, such as checking if an item is available or learning more about the parts you sell.

  - **Operations:** This section helps you handle tasks like creating job orders or setting up estimates and repairs for your work. Under this are operations such as:

| **Name**           | **Description**                                                                                                                                                            |
| ------------------ | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Inspection         | This link is where you can manage vehicle inspections. You might use it to check a vehicle’s condition and record any issues that need to be fixed.                        |
| Estimate           | This section allows you to create estimates for repair or service jobs. You can use it to calculate and share the expected costs with your customers before starting work. |
| Job Order          | This link helps you create and manage job orders. It’s where you can set up tasks for vehicle repairs or services and track their progress.                                |
| Sales Order        | This section is for handling sales orders. You might use it to process orders for parts or services that customers purchase from your shop.                                |
| Quick Sale         | This link lets you quickly record a sale without creating a full job order. It’s useful for fast transactions, like selling a small part or service                        |
| Jobs Board         | This section shows a visual board of all active jobs. It can help you see which tasks are in progress, who’s working on them, and their status.                            |
| Appointments       | This link is for managing appointments. You can use it to schedule customer visits for repairs, services, or inspections.                                                  |
| Warranties         | This section likely helps you manage warranty information. You can track warranties for parts or services and handle any claims or issues.                                 |
| Invoices           | This link is for creating and managing invoices. You can use it to bill customers for completed jobs and keep track of payments.                                           |
| Deposits           | This section is for recording deposits. You can use it to track money paid upfront by customers for jobs or services.                                                      |
| Payments           | This link helps you manage customer payments. You can record payments for invoices and see which ones are still unpaid.                                                    |
| Account Receivable | This section is for tracking money that customers owe you. It helps you manage unpaid invoices and follow up on overdue payments.                                          |
| Expenses           | This link lets you record and manage your shop’s expenses. You can track costs like parts purchases or bank charges to keep your finances in order                         |

  - **Inventory:** Here, you can keep an eye on your stock, ensuring you know what items you have and when you need to restock. Under this are operations such as:

| Stock Quantities  | Use this link to check the current amount of each item in your stock. It helps you see what you have on hand and identify items that might be running low.  |

| Supplier Payments | This section is for managing payments to your suppliers. Use it to record when you pay invoices and keep your accounts up to date.                          |
| Supplier Credits  | This link lets you manage credits from suppliers, such as returns or refunds. It helps you track money owed back to you.                                    |
| Accounts Payable  | Use this section to keep track of money you owe to suppliers. It helps you manage unpaid bills and due dates.                                               |
| Stock Releases    | This link is for releasing stock from inventory for use in jobs or sales. It ensures your stock levels are updated when items are taken out.                |
| Supplier Quotes   | This section allows you to request and manage quotes from suppliers. Use it to compare prices before placing a purchase order.                              |

  - **CRM:** This stands for Customer Relationship Management. It’s a tool to organize your interactions with customers and keep their information in one place. Under this are operations such as:

| **Name**          | **Description**                                                                                                                                                                                          |
| ----------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| SMS Messages      | This link lets you send and manage text messages to your customers. You can use it to notify them about updates, like when their vehicle is ready or to remind them of appointments.                     |
| Service Reminders | This section helps you set up and send reminders to customers about upcoming or overdue vehicle services. It’s a great way to keep customers on track with maintenance and bring them back to your shop. |

  - **People:** This section is likely for managing details about your staff or other contacts, helping you keep track of your team. Under this are operations such as:

| Leave Request    | This link allows employees to submit leave requests. You can review and approve or deny these requests to manage time off effectively.                       |
| Overtime Request | This section is for managing over time requests from your staff. You can review and approve extra hours worked to ensure proper compensation.                |

  - **Accounting:** This area takes care of your shop’s financial tasks, such as tracking money coming in and going out, and managing your income and expenses. Under this are operations such as:

| **Name**                 | **Description**                                                                                                                                    |

| Account Groups           | This section lets you organize accounts into groups, making it easier to manage and view related financial information.                            |

  - **Administration:** This is for administrative tasks, such as setting up user accounts or adjusting system settings, giving you control over how the system works. Under this are operations such as:

| Vehicle Models        | This link helps you add and manage specific vehicle models for each make, ensuring accurate records.                              |
| Inspection Templates  | Use this section to create and manage templates for vehicle inspections, making it easier to perform consistent checks.           |
| Product Groups        | This link allows you to group your products, like parts or accessories, for better organization and tracking.                     |
| Product Categories    | This section helps you categorize products (e.g., brakes, filters) to keep your inventory organized.                              |
| Manufacturers         | Use this link to manage information about the manufacturers of your products or parts, such as brand details.                     |
| Unit of Measure       | This section lets you set up units of measure (e.g., liters, pieces) for your products to ensure accurate tracking.               |
| Parameter Groups      | This link helps you group parameters or settings for customizing how your shop operates, like specific workflows.                 |
| Parameters            | Use this section to adjust individual settings or parameters that control how different parts of the system work.                 |
| Product Pricing       | This link allows you to set and manage prices for your products, ensuring your pricing is up to date.                             |
| User Accounts         | This section lets you create and manage user accounts for your team, controlling who can access the system.                       |
| Roles and Permissions | Use this link to assign roles and set permissions, deciding what each user can do in the system.                                  |
| Locations             | This section helps you manage different shop locations if you have more than one, keeping records organized.                      |
| System Numbers        | This link allows you to manage numbering systems, like invoice or order numbers, for consistency.                                 |
| Warranty Templates    | Use this section to create and manage templates for warranties, making it easy to apply them to parts or services.                |
| Print Templates       | This link lets you set up and manage templates for printing documents, like invoices or reports.                                  |
| Membership            | This section allows you to manage membership programs, offering benefits to regular customers.                                    |

The side panel is simple to use—just click on any section to go to that part of the system. You can collapse it to free up more space on your screen if you need to\!

The preferred browser for using AutoMetrik is **Google Chrome**, as it offers the best performance and compatibility. However, it is also compatible with **Safari** and **Firefox**, providing flexibility across different devices and user preferences.

To streamline access, it's recommended to bookmark the login page and memorize your username on all your devices. This ensures you can log in quickly and efficiently whenever needed. In most cases, a single browser session is sufficient for daily use. However, if you need to access multiple AutoMetrik accounts simultaneously, it can be helpful to open separate user sessions or profiles in Chrome.

Use the following procedure to **manage multiple logins**.

1.  Open Chrome. At the top right, click the button with your name or People.

2.  Click Manage people then Add Person.

3.  Choose a photo and a name.

4.  Click Save. A new window will open and ask you to sign in

5.  Sign into Chrome with a Google Account for the new profile

name: Business Process and System Flow Guide

arts.md:
This guide follows a vehicle, a part and a peso through the system, from the moment a customer books to the moment the money lands in the ledger. Every screen you will use appears somewhere in one of the nine flow charts, and every status a document can carry is listed with what it actually does.

## How to use this Guide
Read Section 2 first — the one-page map of the whole system. After that, each part stands on its own, so you can turn straight to the process you are being trained on.

Three conventions run through the document:

  - **Status names** are written exactly as they appear on screen: *Open*, *In Process*, *Released*.

  - **Stock effects** are called out wherever a step moves inventory, because that is where mistakes are expensive.

  - **Setting** marks behaviour that your branch can turn on or off in Location Settings, so your screens may differ slightly from a colleague's at another branch.

## The system at a glance

Work flows through six layers. You set the business up once, then the day-to-day cycle runs from left to right and top to bottom.

![](articles/images/image8.png)

Figure 1 — The six layers of the system and how documents pass between them

The important thing to notice is that **almost everything ends in an Invoice**. A job order, a sales order and a quick sale are three different ways of getting to the same place, chosen by what the customer needs:

| **The customer needs**       | **Use**     | **Because**                                |
| ---------------------------- | ----------- | ------------------------------------------ |
| Labour, or labour and parts  | Job Order   | It carries mechanics, hours and a vehicle  |
| Parts only, ordered ahead    | Sales Order | Parts are reserved until collection        |
| Parts only, over the counter | Quick Sale  | Payment and hand-over happen at once       |
| A price before committing    | Estimate    | It converts into a Job Order once approved |

## Before you start: the set-up data
Nothing in the operations screens works until the reference data behind it exists. Set it up in this order — each row depends on the ones above it.

| **Set up**                                     | **Where**      | **Why it comes first**                                                      |
| ---------------------------------------------- | -------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Locations, users, roles                        | Administration | Every document belongs to one location; permissions decide what a user sees |
| Parameters and system numbers                  | Administration | Statuses, terms and the reference-number series for each document           |
| Services, service groups, packages             | Administration | Labour lines and their standard hours and rates                             |
| Products, categories, manufacturers            | Inventory      | Parts, part numbers, units and vehicle applications                         |
| Product pricing and pricing tiers              | Administration | Sell prices, price overrides, quantity breaks, tier prices per customer     |
| Suppliers                                      | Inventory      | Needed before a purchase order can be raised                                |
| Vehicle makes, models and inspection templates | Administration | Drive the vehicle picker and the inspection checklist                       |
| Customers and their vehicles                   | Customers      | Can also be created on the fly from a job order                             |

|                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                         |
| --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| **Pricing is layered.** A product's sell price can be overridden by a pricing tier attached to the customer, and again by a quantity break. A service's rate can be overridden by a classification rate tied to the vehicle's model class. The system applies the most specific rule it finds — you do not have to work it out by hand. |

## The cycle end to end

![](articles/images/image6.png)

Figure 2 — From booking to closed job, with the two decision points that change the path

## Customers and vehicles

A vehicle belongs to a customer, and every job order, estimate and inspection is written against a vehicle. If the customer is new, you do not have to leave the job order screen — the plus button beside the Customer field creates the customer, and the plus beside the Vehicle field creates the vehicle against that customer.

When you pick a vehicle, three things happen automatically:

1.  The VIN appears beside the vehicle label.

2.  The customer is filled in, if you started from the vehicle.

3.  If the vehicle has **open inspection items**, a red badge shows the count beside the vehicle label. Click it to see them — see Section 1.4.

## Appointments

Appointments can be booked by your staff or by the customer through the public booking link. They are a diary, not a document — nothing moves in stock or money until a job order is raised.

| **Status** | **Meaning**                                                       |
| ---------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Pending    | Requested through the booking page, not yet confirmed by the shop |
| Scheduled  | Confirmed and on the calendar                                     |
| Attended   | The customer arrived; a job order is normally raised now          |
| No Show    | The customer did not arrive                                       |
| Cancelled  | Called off by either side                                         |

Appointment reminders and service reminders are configured separately under CRM and go out by SMS on the schedule you set.

## Vehicle inspection

An inspection is a checklist run against a template. The mechanic marks every item with one of three findings:

| **Finding**                  | **Shown as** | **What it means**           |
| ---------------------------- | ------------ | --------------------------- |
| Okay                         | no marker    | Nothing to do               |
| May Require Attention        | orange dot   | Should be watched or quoted |
| Requires Immediate Attention | red dot      | Should be fixed now         |

Items that are not *Okay* and not yet completed are **pending inspection items**. They stay attached to the vehicle until somebody deals with them, which is what makes them useful months later.

**Working the pending items from a job order or estimate.** Select the vehicle, then click the red badge beside the Vehicle field. A window lists every pending item with the mechanic's notes and the needed service. Each row has two buttons:

  - **Add** — copies the item's needed service into the Labour section of the job order or estimate, at the correct rate and standard hours.

  - **Done** — marks the inspection item completed, with a date and remarks, exactly as the Vehicle → Inspections screen does. The badge count drops as you go.

An item with no needed service set can still be marked *Done*, but there is nothing to add — set a needed service on the inspection item if you want it to be quotable.

## Estimates

An estimate is a quotation. It looks and behaves like a job order, but it reserves nothing and bills nothing.

![Estimate flow](articles/images/image2.png)

Figure 3 — The life of an estimate

Steps:

1.  Create the estimate against the customer and vehicle. Add services, parts and packages. Use the magnifier on the **Parts & Materials** header to search the catalogue by name, part number, manufacturer or category — and tick *Filter by Estimate Vehicle* to see only parts that fit the car in front of you.

2.  Set the validity date. After that date the estimate shows as expired.

3.  Send it — print, e-mail or SMS.

4.  When the customer approves, convert it to a job order. Every service and part line is copied across.

## Job orders

The job order is the centre of the system. It carries the vehicle, the labour, the parts, the mechanics and the money.

![Job order statuses](articles/images/image11.png)

Figure 4 — Job order statuses. Parts are reserved on save and only deducted on release

| **Status** | **What has happened**                        | **Effect on stock**                                                  |
| ---------- | -------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Open       | The job order is saved with its lines        | Parts are **allocated** — available quantity drops, on-hand does not |
| In Process | Work has started; mechanics clock in and out | No change                                                            |
| Completed  | The work is finished and checked             | No change                                                            |
| Released   | The vehicle is handed to the customer        | Parts are **deducted** from on-hand and the allocation is cleared    |
| Cancelled  | The job is called off before release         | Allocations are released back                                        |

**Raising the job order**

1.  Pick the customer and the vehicle. Deal with any pending inspection items (Section 1.4).

2.  Add labour under **Labour**: choose the service, the mechanic, and the hours. The rate defaults from the service, adjusted for the vehicle's classification where classification rates are switched on.

3.  Add parts under **Parts & Materials**. Type the name or part number, or use the magnifier for the advanced search — filter by manufacturer, category or the vehicle's own applications, and add straight from the results.

4.  Apply a package if one fits — the package's services and parts are added in one step.

5.  Save. Availability for every part drops immediately, so nobody else can promise the same stock.

**Running the job**

Move the job to *In Process* when a mechanic starts. Mechanics clock in and out against the job order; those hours feed the Mechanic Jobs report, the incentive calculation and the payroll time sheet. The Jobs Board shows every open job as a column so the service advisor can see the floor at a glance.

**Finishing**

Move the job to *Completed* when the work is done. Then raise the invoice — the invoice window offers a *Release job order* tick box, which is the normal way to move the job to *Released* in the same step.

|                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    |
| ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| **Two settings change the end of this flow.** *Restrict released items* requires the stock releases for a job to match the parts on it before the job can be completed. *Allow released with no invoice* decides whether a job can be released without an invoice at all. Ask your supervisor which way your branch is configured. |

On release the system sends the customer's feedback link and, where SMS is enabled, the released notification. Reverting a released job back to *Completed* puts the parts back into stock — it is a genuine reversal, not a cosmetic one.

![Sales order and quick sale](articles/images/image4.png)

Figure 5 — The two parts-only routes

**Sales Order** is for parts a customer orders ahead. *Open* captures the order, *Confirmed* reserves the parts against the customer, and *Completed* deducts the stock and raises the invoice. Cancelling releases the reservation.

**Quick Sale** is the counter till. Items are added, payment is taken, and completing the sale deducts stock and prints the receipt in one action. Cancelling a completed quick sale reverses both the stock and the payment.

Both screens have the same advanced product search as the job order, so a counter staff member can find a part by manufacturer or category without knowing the part number.

![Invoice and payment](articles/images/image1.png)

Figure 6 — Invoice statuses and how payment moves them

| **Status**     | **Meaning**                                                         |
| -------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Draft          | Prepared but not yet posted                                         |
| Open           | Posted and due; the due date comes from the customer's payment term |
| Partially Paid | Some payment received, a balance remains                            |
| Fully Paid     | The balance is zero                                                 |
| Cancelled      | Voided                                                              |

**Raising an invoice from a job order.** Open the job order and choose *Create Invoice*. The window carries over the customer, the amounts, the prepared-by name and the remarks, and lets you set the invoice number and date. Tick *Release job order* if the vehicle is going out now. **Setting** — where an invoice approver is required, the approver is selected here; where the invoice date is locked, you cannot back-date it.

**Deposits.** A deposit taken earlier is applied when the invoice is raised and reduces the balance due.

**Payments.** A payment can be cash, cheque, card or a mix, and one payment can settle several invoices at once. Cheques are tracked separately through the check register — *For Clearing*, then *Cleared* or *Cancelled*.

**Accounts Receivable.** Every unpaid or partly paid invoice appears in the AR ageing report, grouped by how long it has been outstanding. Statement of Account prints the same information for one customer.

![Purchasing cycle](articles/images/image7.png)

Figure 7 — From a purchase order to a paid supplier, and how returns come back

## Purchase orders

| **Status**         | **Meaning**                                    |
| ------------------ | ---------------------------------------------- |
| New Request        | Drafted, not yet submitted                     |
| For Approval       | Waiting on the approver                        |
| Approved / Ordered | Released to the supplier                       |
| Acknowledged       | The supplier has confirmed the order           |
| Partially Received | Some lines received against a purchase receipt |
| Delivered          | Everything ordered has been received           |
| Closed             | No further receipts expected                   |
| Declined           | The approver rejected it                       |
| Cancelled          | Withdrawn                                      |

A purchase order can be raised for stock, or for a specific job order when a part has to be bought in for one car.

## Receiving

A **Purchase Receipt** is what actually raises stock. Receive against the purchase order, check the quantities and the cost, and the on-hand quantity goes up and the moving cost is recalculated. Receiving part of an order moves it to *Partially Received*; receiving the rest moves it to *Delivered*.

## Paying the supplier

The **Supplier Invoice** records what the supplier is charging. The **Supplier Payment** settles it. Anything unsettled shows in the Accounts Payable ageing report.

## Returns and credits

A **Purchase Return** (*New Request* → *Approved*, or *Cancelled*) sends goods back and takes them out of stock. The supplier's **Credit** note is then recorded (*Open* → *Approved*) and applied against later invoices, moving through *Partially Applied* to *Fully Applied*.

## Controlling stock

| **Document**     | **Statuses**                                                            | **Use it when**                                                      |
| ---------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Stock Adjustment | New Request → Approved, or Cancelled                                    | Stock is written off or corrected — defective, stolen, opening stock |
| Stock Transfer   | New Request → Approved → Shipped / Sent → Received; Denied or Cancelled | Stock moves between branches                                         |
| Stock Release    | New Request → Released, or Cancelled                                    | Parts are physically issued from the store to a job                  |
| Cycle Count      | counted, then posted                                                    | A shelf is recounted and the system is corrected                     |

Every product holds three numbers at every location. Getting these three straight prevents most inventory arguments.

| **Number** | **What it is**                                       |
| ---------- | ---------------------------------------------------- |
| On hand    | What is physically on the shelf                      |
| Allocated  | What is promised to open job orders and sales orders |
| Available  | On hand minus allocated — what you may still promise |

![Stock movement map](articles/images/image3.png)

Figure 8 — Which documents raise stock, which reserve it, and which deduct it

The rule worth memorising: **saving a job order reserves; releasing it deducts.** A part sitting on an open job order is still on the shelf but is no longer available to sell — which is exactly why the counter shows a lower number than the shelf does.

![Payroll cycle](articles/images/image10.png)

Figure 9 — From the employee record to the payslip

Mechanic hours are captured on the job order itself, so the same clock-in serves three purposes: it tells the service advisor where the job is, it feeds the incentive calculation, and it fills the payroll time sheet.

Leave and overtime requests follow a simple approval path — *New*, then *Approved*, *Denied* or *Cancelled*. Payroll is then run for a payroll group over its period, which may be weekly, every two weeks, twice a month or monthly.

Operational documents post into the books; you do not journalise sales by hand.

| **Journal**               | **Fed by**                           |
| ------------------------- | ------------------------------------ |
| Sales Journal             | Invoices and quick sales             |
| Purchase Journal          | Supplier invoices                    |
| Cash Receipt Journal      | Customer payments and deposits       |
| Cash Disbursement Journal | Supplier payments, expenses, payroll |
| General Journal           | Manual entries and adjustments       |

From these come the Trial Balance, the General Ledger and the three statements — Income Statement, Balance Sheet and Cash Flow Statement.

The Reports menu is organised by question rather than by module: sales by product or service, daily collections, mechanic jobs and clock in/out, vehicles due for service, top customers, top suppliers, and the loyalty and incentive reports.

| **Tool**                   | **What it does**                                                                           |
| -------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |

| Appointment Reminders      | Sent ahead of a scheduled appointment                                                      |
| SMS Messages and Campaigns | One-off messages, or a campaign that moves *Draft* → *Scheduled* → *Running* → *Completed* |
| Promotions and Membership  | Discount schemes and loyalty points earned on invoices                                     |

| **Document**                     | **Statuses in order**                                                                                                           |
| -------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Appointment                      | Pending · Scheduled · Attended · No Show · Cancelled                                                                            |
| Job Order                        | Open · In Process · Completed · Released · Cancelled                                                                            |
| Estimate                         | Open until converted, or expired on its validity date                                                                           |

| Purchase Order                   | New Request · For Approval · Approved / Ordered · Acknowledged · Partially Received · Delivered · Closed · Declined · Cancelled |
| Purchase Return                  | New Request · Approved · Cancelled                                                                                              |
| Supplier Credit                  | Open · Approved · Partially Applied · Fully Applied · Cancelled                                                                 |
| Supplier Payment                 | New · Completed · Cancelled                                                                                                     |

arts.t: How to Log In and Out
arts.md:

2.  Enter your **Username** and **Password**, then select **Sign In**.

Use the following procedure to **log out** on your account.

1.  On the upper-right corner of your screen, click the **User Profile section**.

2.  Click **Sign out** to log out.

The AutoMetrik Dashboard is **the main page you see when you log into the system**. It gives you a quick and easy look at how your auto shop is doing. Here’s a simple breakdown of what you’ll see:

  - **Job Orders:** This section shows the number of job orders in your shop. It helps you see how many repair or service tasks are active.

  - **Customers**: This part displays the number of customers you’re working with. It keeps track of who’s coming to your shop.

  - **Inventory**: This section shows how many items you have in stock, like parts and accessories, and highlights any that are low.

  - **Vehicles**: This area tells you how many vehicles are in your shop, including those being worked on or waiting.

  - **Profit & Loss**: This gives a quick summary of your shop’s money. It shows your revenue (money coming in) and expenses (money going out) for the month, so you can see if you’re making a profit.

  - **Cash In/Out**: This section tracks the cash moving in and out of your shop, helping you see your daily cash flow.

  - **Accounts**: This part shows your financial accounts, like cash in the bank, to give you an idea of your available funds.

  - **Revenue Breakdown**: This is a chart that breaks down where your money is coming from, like parts sales or service income, so you know what’s bringing in the most.

  - **Expenses Breakdown**: This chart shows where your money is going, like costs for parts or bank fees, helping you manage spending.

  - **6-Month Sales**: This graph shows your sales over the last six months, so you can see trends and how your business is growing.

The dashboard is the main screen you see when you log in. It’s divided into sections with colorful tiles and charts that give you a quick look at your shop’s performance. Here’s what you’ll find:

  - **Top Bar**: At the top, you’ll see the website address (app.autometric.ph) and open tabs like "Auto Shop Office - Dashboard."

| **Name**           | **Description**                                                                               |
| ------------------ | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |

| Expenses Breakdown | A blue pie chart showing where your money goes (e.g., Cost of Sale, Bank Charges).            |
| 6-Month Sales      | A line graph on the right showing sales trends over the last six months.                      |

  - **User Panel**: On the top right, there’s a panel with your username membership details and options like Account Settings and Sign Out.

On the left side, there’s a collapsible menu with icons and sections to help you navigate the system. Click any section to expand it and access its features. Here’s how to use it:

| **Name**        | **Description**                                                                                                |
| --------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Company Logo    | At the top, the logo takes you back to the main dashboard.                                                     |
| Dashboard       | This section (highlighted when active) shows the overview you’re currently viewing.                            |

| Customers       | Use this to view and manage customer details and records.                                                      |
|                 |                                                                                                                |

arts.t: How to Import Existing Data of Customers
arts.md:
Use the following procedure to **import data on your account**.

1.  Click on the **Customers** option in the left menu to open the customer management page.

2.  Look for the **Import** button at the top right of the customer list and **click it**. This will take you to the Import Customers page.

3.  Ensure your customer data is in a **compatible format**, such as a CSV file. Include columns like Name, Code, Vehicles, Email, and Contact Date.

\[***NOTE*** : If your file is not in a compatible format, download a template by clicking **Download Template** on the import page to match the required format.\]

4\. Click the **Choose File** button and browse your computer to select the prepared CSV file containing your customer data.

5\. Click the **Preview** button to review the data that will be imported. Check for any errors or mismatches.

6\. If the preview looks correct, click **Import** **to upload the data** into the system. Wait for a confirmation message to ensure the process is successful.

7\. Return to the customer list by clicking **Back to List** and check that all customers from your file are now displayed.

Use the following procedure to **export data on your account.**

1.  Click on the **Customers** option in the left menu to open the customer management page.

2.  Look for the **Export** button at the top right of the customer list and click it. This will download a CSV file containing all current customer data.

3.  Choose a location on your computer to **save the downloaded file** and name it as needed.

4.  **Open the exported CSV file** using a spreadsheet program (like Excel) to verify that it includes all customer details, such as names, codes, vehicles, emails, and contact dates.

5.  **Use the exported file for backups**, sharing with other systems, or analyzing customer information outside the AutoMetrik platform.

arts.t: How to Import Templates and Format Guidelines
arts.md:
An Import Template is **a pre-made file (like a CSV) provided by the system** that shows the exact structure you need for your data. It includes column headers (e.g., Name, Code, Email) to match the fields in AutoMetrik. It ensures your data fits the system’s requirements, making the import process easier and reducing errors.

Use the following procedure to **import template**.

1.  Go to the **Import** section (e.g., under Customers).

2.  Click **Download Template to** get the file.

3.  **Fill in your data** (e.g., customer names, contact info) under the correct columns using Google Sheets or Excel, then upload it using the Choose File option.

Format Guidelines are specific rules about how your data should be organized in the template. They tell you what kind of information goes in each column and how it should be written. Following these rules prevents mistakes during import, like mismatched data or missing fields.

Examples of Guidelines:

  - **Name:** Enter full names (e.g., "John Doe") with no extra spaces.

  - **Code:** Use a unique code (e.g., "CUST-001") for each entry.

  - **Email:** Include valid email addresses (e.g., "john@example.com").

  - **Date:** Use a standard format (e.g., MM-DD-YYYY) for dates like contact dates.

  - **Required Fields:** Some columns (like Name) must be filled; others (like Email) might be optional.

\[***NOTE***: Always check the guidelines (often provided on the import page or in the template instructions) before filling your file. Stick to these rules to ensure a successful import.\]

arts.t: How to Access Initial Configuration Wizard
arts.md:
It is a tool that walks you through the **basic setup process** to get the system ready for your business. It covers essential settings like user accounts, shop details, and service categories. It makes setup easy by guiding you through each step, ensuring you don’t miss anything important. This helps you start using the system quickly and correctly.

  - **Set Up Your Shop**: Enter basic info like your shop’s name, address, and contact details.

  - **Add Users**: Create accounts for yourself and your team, assigning roles like manager or mechanic.

  - **Define Services**: Set up the types of services your shop offers, such as oil changes or tire repairs.

  - **Configure Preferences**: Choose settings like currency, time zone, or invoice numbering.

  - **Add Initial Data**: Optionally import or enter starting data, like a list of products or customers.

**Qonnec will host a User Orientation for clients** after they avail of AutoMetrik, either through **virtual meeting or face-to-face setting**. This orientation ensures that clients are properly introduced to the system and understand how it works. In addition, the company will provide a user manual and access to an online support site at **https://autometrik.freshdesk.com/support/home**, where clients can find answers to common questions or get help if they encounter any issues by submitting a ticket.

arts.t: How to Setup Branch or Location
arts.md:
The Branch or Location Setup in the AutoMetrik system allows you **to manage multiple branches or locations** for your auto shop, ensuring all sites are organized and tracked efficiently. It helps you keep track of inventory, customers, and operations across all locations, making it easier to manage a multi-branch business.

Use the following procedure to **setup a branch**.

1.  **Access the Dashboard**: Log in to the Auto Shop Office application and navigate to the main dashboard, where key metrics like revenue, expenses, customers, inventory, and vehicles are displayed.

2.  **Locate the Select Location Dropdown**: In the upper left corner of the dashboard, find the "Select Location" button or dropdown menu (it may appear as a blue bar with the current location name).

3.  **Click to Open the Dropdown**: Click on the "Select Location" button to expand the list of available branches. This will show all branches associated with your account.

4.  **Choose a Branch**: Scroll through the list if necessary and click on the desired branch to select it. The dashboard will refresh to display data and settings specific to that branch.

5.  **Verify Selection**: Confirm the selected branch is now shown in the dropdown (e.g., updated to the new branch name), and review the dashboard metrics to ensure they reflect the chosen branch's information.

6.  **Edit Branch Settings (Optional)**: If needed, go to "Administration" in the left sidebar, then select "Locations" to edit settings for the selected or any other branch.

\[***NOTE***: Qonnec provides the initial accounts for each branch, but users can customize settings like branding, print templates, tax, discounts, inventory, and other configurations per branch.\]

arts.t: How to Configure the System for the First Time
arts.md:
The Initial System Configuration in the AutoMetrik system is the **process of setting up the platform to match your auto shop’s specific needs when you first start using it**. This ensures the system is ready for daily operations. It tailors the system to your shop’s structure, making it easier to manage customers, jobs, inventory, and finances from day one.

Use the following procedure to **configure the system for the first time**.

1.  **Start the Configuration**: Log in for the first time. The system may launch an Initial Configuration Wizard automatically, or you can find it under the Administration section.

2.  **Follow the Steps**: Go through each screen, entering required details like shop info and user accounts.

3.  **Set Up Services and Products**: Add your service categories and product types as prompted.

4.  **Configure Finances**: Input your preferred financial settings, such as currency or tax options.

5.  **Add Locations**: If applicable, set up multiple branches or locations.

6.  **Import Data**: Use the import tool to upload existing records (e.g., customers, inventory).

7.  **Save and Review**: Click "Finish" or "Save" to complete the setup, then check the dashboard to ensure everything is correct.

1.  **Access the Dashboard**: Log in to the system and navigate to the main dashboard, where key metrics like revenue, expenses, customers, inventory, and vehicles are displayed.

2.  **Locate the Select Location Dropdown**: In the upper left corner of the dashboard, find the "Select Location" button or dropdown menu (it may appear as a blue bar with the current location name).

3.  **Click to Open the Dropdown**: Click on the "Select Location" button to expand the list of available branches. This will show all branches associated with your account.

4.  **Edit Current Branch Settings**: Select the “Settings” button at the bottom left of the dropdown menu. This will take you to the three main navigations of your branch information: **Location**, **Print Settings**, and **Other Settings**.

\[***NOTE***: **Location Settings** contains information about your current branch, **Print Settings** is for your branch printable templates, and **Other Settings** is for administrative settings of your branch.\]

5\. **Scroll Through the Sections**: (Header, Estimate, Job Order, Invoice, Quick Sale, etc.). For each document type you want to customize. For Quick Sale, Payment, Deposit, Purchase Order, etc.: Keep titles simple and footers minimal (or leave blank if not used).

6\. **Save Your Edit**: Scroll to bottom, click **Save** / **Update**. Wait for confirmation.

7\. **Test Printing Templates**: Go to Vehicles or Operations and create a test Job Order / Estimate / Invoice. Click Print/Preview to check header, terms, signatures, footer appearance. Return to Print Settings to adjust if needed.

The AutoMetrik system makes it easy to **add and edit vehicle records**, helping you keep track of all vehicles your auto shop services. It keeps all vehicle details in one place, making it easier to manage jobs, track history, and schedule services.

Use the following procedure to **add a vehicle**.

1.  **Navigate to Vehicles**: Click on the "Vehicles" option in the left menu to open the vehicle management page.

2.  **Add a New Vehicle**: Look for a "New" or "Add Vehicle" button (usually at the top right) and click it.

3.  **Enter Vehicle Details**: Fill in the required fields, such as:
    
      - **Make**: The vehicle’s brand (e.g., Toyota).
    
      - **Model**: The specific model (e.g., Corolla).
    
      - **Year**: The vehicle’s manufacturing year.
    
      - **License Plate**: The vehicle’s plate number.

4.  **Save the Record**: Click "Save" or "Submit" to add the vehicle to the system.

5.  **Verify**: Go back to the vehicle list to ensure the new vehicle appears.

3.  **Open the Record**: Click on the vehicle’s name or an "Edit" button next to it to open its details.

4.  **Update Details**: Make changes to fields like the customer, license plate, or other information as needed.

5.  **Save Changes**: Click "Save" or "Update" to confirm your changes.

6.  **Verify**: Check the vehicle list to ensure the updates are reflected.

arts.t: How to Link Vehicle to a Customer
arts.md:
Linking vehicles to customers means **connecting a vehicle record to the customer who owns or uses it** in the system. This ties all related information together, like service history and contact details. It helps you quickly see which customer owns a vehicle, manage their service requests, and keep accurate records for billing or communication.

Use the following procedure to **link a vehicle**.

1.  **Navigate to Vehicles:** Click on the "Vehicles" option in the left menu to open the vehicle management page.

2.  **Add or Edit a Vehicle:**
    
      - **For a New Vehicle:** Click "New" or "Add Vehicle" to create a new record.
    
      - **For an Existing Vehicle:** Find the vehicle in the list and click "Edit" to open its details.

<!-- end list -->

3.  **Select the Customer:**
    
      - In the "Customer Information" section, use the "Customer" dropdown or type-in field.
    
      - Start typing the customer’s name to search, then select the correct name from the list that appears.
    
      - If the customer isn’t listed, add them first under the "Customers" section before linking.

<!-- end list -->

Product maintenance refers to the process of regularly updating, managing, and optimizing product information and related data within an inventory or management system. This includes adjusting details such as product names, part numbers, pricing, stock levels, supplier information, unit conversions, vehicle associations, and transaction records to ensure accuracy and relevance.

**Why is it Important?**

  - **Accuracy**: Keeps product data current, reducing errors in orders, pricing, and inventory tracking.

  - **Efficiency**: Streamlines operations by ensuring all teams (e.g., sales, procurement) work with the latest information.

  - **Customer Satisfaction**: Provides accurate product details to customers, enhancing trust and service quality.

  - **Cost Management**: Helps monitor costs and adjust pricing or stock levels to maintain profitability.

  - **Compliance**: Ensures adherence to inventory and regulatory requirements through updated records.

Use the following procedure to **check products**.

1.  **Navigate to the Products Section**: On the left sidebar, locate and click on the "Inventory" menu to expand it. Then, click on "Products" under Inventory. This will display the main Products list page.

2.  **Select the Product to Maintain**: In the Products list, use the search bar at the top right to find the specific product. Click on the product's name in the table to open its detailed view.

3.  **Update Product Information (Product Info Tab):**

<!-- end list -->

  - The page defaults to the "Product Info" tab.

  - Edit fields in the "Product Information" section, such as Name, Part No, Product Group, Print Display Name, Category, Unit of Measure, Description, Manufacturer, Manufacturer No, Color, Expiry Date, Serialized, Display Notes, and Incentive.

  - Scroll down to the "Price Information" section and update Purchase Cost, Product Pricing, Markup Rate, and Sell Price.

  - In the "Inventory Details" section, toggle "Track Inventory" if needed, then edit Re-Order Point, Safety Stock Level, Storage Location, Min Order, Order Multiple, Initial Quantity, and As-Of Date.

  - Once edits are complete, click the blue "Save Product" button at the bottom to apply changes.

4\. **Configure** **Units (Units Tab):**

  - Click on the "Units" tab.

5\. **Add or Edit Suppliers (Suppliers Tab):**

6\. **Associate Vehicles (Vehicles Tab):**

  - Click on the "Vehicles" tab.

  - If the table is empty, click "New" to link the product to vehicles.

  - Enter details in columns like Vehicle, Year Model, and Date.

7\. **Review Transactions (Transactions Tab):**

  - Click on the "Transactions" tab.

  - View the history table with columns like Reference No, Transaction Type, Customer/Supplier/Employee, Quantity, Price, Inventory, and Date.

  - Use the filter button to search or sort transactions. This tab is read-only for review.

Use the following procedure to **update the product details**.

Use the following procedure to **update the product pricing.**

1.  Click **Inventory** on the menu.

2.  Select **Products** from the submenu.

3.  **Choose a product** from the list to open its details.

4.  Find the Price Information and **adjust the Purchase Cost** as needed.

5.  **Choose a pricing method** from the dropdown.

<!-- end list -->

  - **FIXED**: Allows you to set a fixed sell price regardless of the purchase cost, providing control over pricing without automatic adjustments. For example, the sell price is manually set to 25.00 PC with a 20.00% margin.

  - **FIXED with OVERRIDE**: Similar to FIXED, but includes an override feature, enabling manual adjustments to the fixed price when needed, offering flexibility for special cases.

  - **MARK-UP 20 W/ OVERRIDE**: Applies a 20% markup on the purchase cost (20.00 PC) to calculate the sell price, with the option to manually override the result if required.

  - **MARK-UP 30**: Adds a 30% markup to the purchase cost, automatically setting the sell price based on this percentage without override capability.

  - **MARK-UP 35:** Increases the purchase cost by 35% to determine the sell price, providing a higher profit margin option.

  - **MARK-UP 35 WHOLESALE**: Applies a 35% markup tailored for wholesale pricing, potentially differing from retail calculations.

  - **MARK-UP 40**: Adds a 40% markup to the purchase cost, suitable for higher-margin products.

  - **MARK-UP 40 W/ AUTO UPDATE**: Applies a 40% markup with automatic updates to the sell price if the purchase cost changes, ensuring real-time pricing adjustments.

  - **Tiered Pricing**: Offers a tiered pricing structure, allowing different sell prices based on quantity or customer type, though specific tiers would need to be configured separately.

6\. Set the Markup Rate percentage to automatically calculate the sell price, or manually enter a Sell Price to see the resulting margin.

7\. **Save changes** by clicking "Save Product."

The customer workflow in AutoMetrik **manages the entire customer journey**, from inquiry to job completion and payment, ensuring efficient service delivery and accurate record-keeping. This process integrates with inventory, operations, and accounting modules to provide a cohesive experience, leveraging the FIFO inventory method for parts allocation and cost tracking.

The customer workflow in AutoMetrik involves:

  - **Inquiry and Estimate**: Capture customer needs and provide cost estimates.

  - **Job Order Creation**: Schedule and allocate parts using FIFO inventory.

  - **Service Execution**: Perform repairs, consuming parts and logging labor.

  - **Invoicing**: Bill customers, recognizing revenue and FIFO-based COGS.

  - **Payment**: Collect payment and clear receivables.

  - **Follow-Up**: Update customer records and schedule future services.

arts.t: How Estimate to Job Order Works
arts.md:
| **Name**  | **Description**                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                             |
| --------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Estimate  | Accessed under the Operations menu on the left-hand side, the Estimate feature **allows users to create detailed cost projections for vehicle repairs or services**. Users input customer details, vehicle information, and a list of required services or parts. The system calculates an estimated cost, which is then presented to the customer for approval. This step serves as the initial planning phase, helping to set expectations and secure customer consent before proceeding. |
| Job Order | Once an estimate is approved, it transitions into a Job Order under the same Operations menu. This process **involves converting the estimate into an actionable work order, assigning it to a technician, and scheduling the task**. The dashboard displays active job orders, allowing real-time tracking of status, progress, and completion.                                                                                                                                            |

1.  **Creating an Estimate**:

<!-- end list -->

  - You start by filling out the "New Estimate" form with details such as customer name, vehicle information, service advisor, mileage, and estimated days.

  - You add labor services (e.g., "Temperature Sending Unit Replacement" and "AC High Pressure Hose Replacement") with their respective rates, hours, and amounts.

  - Optionally, you can add parts and materials with part numbers, prices, quantities, and amounts.

  - The system calculates the total estimated cost based on the entered data.

2\. **Saving the Estimate**:

  - Once saved (as indicated by the "Save Successful" message), the estimate is stored with a reference number (e.g., EST0001238) and includes the date, expiry date, and other details.

3\. **Converting to a Job Order**:

  - The system allows you to create a new job order based on the saved estimate by clicking the “Convert to Job Order” in the Estimate details.

  - You may assign mechanics to each labor task and add notes or additional details.

  - The system updates the status (e.g., "Open") and generates a new reference number (e.g., RO0001348).

4\. **Processing the Job Order**:

  - After creating the job order, you can further modify it by adding more services, parts, or notes. The "Job Order / Details" view shows the saved information, including labor amounts, parts (e.g., "145/65R15 72S DUNLOP SPOR T2030"), and a summary with subtotals, VAT, and net amounts.

  - The job order can then be tracked through different statuses (e.g., In-Process, Completed, Released) and used to create purchase requests or deposits if needed.

In summary, **creating an estimate sets up a preliminary cost breakdown**, which **can** then **be converted** into a **job order to initiate and manage the actual repair process**, carrying over relevant details for efficiency.

3\. **Automatic Journal Entry:**

2.  Credit Revenue for the service amount, and credit product sales to the respective inventory or sales account.

2.  Debit Cash or the respective payment method account.

<!-- end list -->

  - **Verification**: Journal entries are automatically logged in the "Accounting" section under the respective dates, ensuring accurate financial tracking without manual input.

In summary, **creating an invoice establishes a detailed billing record, which can then be processed through payment recording to finalize transactions and update financial accounts**, with **automatic journal entries** ensuring seamless and accurate tracking.

In summary, **the vehicle release process finalizes the Job Order by confirming service completion, payment, and release details**, while generating Service Reminders to ensure future maintenance is scheduled efficiently.

arts.t: How Service Reminders and Follow-Up Works
arts.md:
Accessed under the Operations menu on the left-hand side, the Optional Follow-ups feature includes **Service Reminders and Warranty options to maintain customer relationships and ensure vehicle upkeep.** For Service Reminders, users can set a future date to notify customers of recommended maintenance, accessible via the Appointments or Vehicles section, helping to schedule timely follow-up services and enhance vehicle performance. For Warranty, users can link warranty details to completed job orders under the Warranties option, tracking coverage periods and notifying customers of warranty expirations or claims. These features, integrated with the dashboard’s revenue and expense data, encourage repeat business and ensure compliance with service agreements.

1.  **Verify Service Reminder Settings**:

<!-- end list -->

  - Ensure Service Reminders are enabled in the system settings to allow automatic generation of reminders for services with defined Next Service Dates (e.g., Change Oil due +3 months from service date).

  - Confirm the preferred notification channels (e.g., SMS, Email, In-app) are configured for customer communication.

2\. **Review Generated Service Reminders**:

  - Access the "Service Reminders" section in the system, typically found in the Operations menu or a dedicated reminders tab.

  - Check the list of automatically generated reminders, which include:
    
    1.  Customer name and contact details.
    
    2.  Vehicle details (make, model, plate number).
    
    3.  Service type (e.g., Change Oil) and target due date (e.g., 2025-10-21 for a service completed on 2025-07-21).
    
    4.  Notification channel selected.

3\. **Send Initial Reminder Notifications**:

  - Trigger the system to send reminders to customers via the configured notification channel.

  - Example SMS Notification:  
    *Hi John Dela Cruz, your Toyota Vios (ABC-1234) is due for a Change Oil service on 2025-10-21. Please book your appointment at ABC Auto Repair. Call 0917-123-4567. Thank you\!*

  - Ensure the notification is sent at the appropriate time (e.g., one week before the due date or as per system settings).

4\. **Track Customer Responses**:

  - Monitor the "Service Reminders" section for customer replies or booking confirmations (e.g., through In-app responses or direct calls).

  - Update the reminder status in the system (e.g., "Acknowledged," "Booking Scheduled," or "No Response").

5\. **Follow Up on Unresponsive Customers**:

  - If no response is received within a set period (e.g., 3 days after the initial reminder), send a follow-up notification via the same or an alternative channel (e.g., Email if SMS was used initially).

  - Example Follow-Up Email:  
    *Dear John Dela Cruz, this is a reminder that your Toyota Vios (ABC-1234) is due for a Change Oil service on 2025-10-21. Please schedule your appointment by contacting ABC Auto Repair at 0917-123-4567 or through our app. Thank you\!*

  - Log the follow-up attempt in the system.

6\. **Assist with Appointment Scheduling**:

  - If the customer responds and requests an appointment, assist in scheduling the service through the system or by coordinating with the service advisor.

  - Create a new estimate or job order linked to the reminder, carrying over relevant details (e.g., customer, vehicle, and service type).

7\. **Update Reminder Status**:

  - Once the customer books an appointment or the service is completed, update the reminder status to "Completed" or "Scheduled" in the system.

  - If the customer declines the service, mark the reminder as "Declined" and add any relevant remarks (e.g., "Customer postponed service").

8\. **Log Follow-Up Activities**:

  - Ensure all follow-up actions (e.g., notifications sent, customer responses, or appointment scheduling) are logged in the system under the respective Service Reminder entry.

  - Verify that the system automatically updates related records (e.g., customer history or upcoming job orders) for accurate tracking.

In summary, the **service reminder follow-up process ensures timely customer communication for upcoming maintenance, tracks responses, and facilitates appointment scheduling** to maintain vehicle care efficiency.

AutoMetrik offers **predefined bundles of services** or products that can be offered to customers to streamline job orders and enhance efficiency. These **packages combine related labor tasks, parts, or maintenance procedures into a single offering, allowing for quicker selection and application during the job order creation process**. They are implemented to simplify the workflow for service advisors and mechanics by reducing the need to manually input individual services or products, ensuring consistency in pricing and service delivery, and providing customers with clear, cost-effective options. Additionally, packages facilitate better inventory management and tracking, as they can be tied to specific parts and quantities, while also enabling the application of discounts or incentives to encourage sales, ultimately improving customer satisfaction and operational productivity.

arts.t: How to Create and Manage Packages
arts.md:
Packages are **pre-defined sets of jobs and parts** (also called “canned jobs”) that can be applied quickly when creating estimates or job orders.  
They are often used for common services such as **oil change**, **brake service**, or **tune-up**, and can include **discounted rates** for bundled items.

When adding parts to a package, you can:

  - **Select a specific product** (e.g., “Engine Oil – Brand X 4L”).

  - **Select a category** (e.g., “Oil Filter”) so the system will prompt you to choose a specific item during estimate or job order creation.
    
      - This is useful when the part varies depending on the car (e.g., different oil filters for different models).
    
      - When a category is used, Autometrik will look for items under that category in your inventory.

## Viewing Existing Packages
1.  Click **Administration** on the menu.

2.  Select **Packages** from the submenu.

3.  Review the list of packages, which includes:
    
      - **Name** – Package description.
    
      - **Amount** – Total cost of the package.
    
      - **Date** – Date of creation or last update.

## Creating a New Package
1.  Click **Administration** on the menu.

2.  Select **Packages** from the submenu.

3.  Click the **New** button (top right).

4.  **Fill in the Package Info:**
    
      - **Name:** Enter the package name (e.g., “New Brake Service Package”).
    
      - **Code:** Assign a unique code (e.g., “BP01”).

5.  **Configure Line Items Printout Options:  
    **These settings control how the package details appear on printed estimates or job orders.
    
      - **Hide Services:** Hides the list of services in the printout (only the package name and total will be shown).
    
      - **Hide Parts & Materials:** Hides the list of parts and materials in the printout.
    
      - **Display Code:** Shows the package code in the printout — useful when multiple packages are used in one job order so you can identify each one.
    
      - **Hide Amounts:** Hides the individual amounts for each service/part so that only the **total package amount** is shown.
    
      - **Replacement Text:** Optional text that will appear in place of the hidden details (if applicable).

6.  **Add Services (optional):**
    
      - Under **Labor**, click **+ Add Service**.
    
      - Type or select a service name.
    
      - Set the **Rate** and **Hours**, then the amount will be calculated automatically.

7.  **Add Parts & Materials (optional):**
